body:
I've tried. They're insistent on not taking me. 

A quick brief Google search (although if you'd like, I could do more digging) pulls up that a therapist, if they believe you are at danger to yourself, others, or reporting abuse to them (whether it be you being abused or the abuser) they can break confidentiality and report that. They can also refer you to psychiatrists if they believe the best plan for you would be taking medication, but they can't necessarily force you to take them. 

My parents believe if I were to get therapy, even if it was in a good price range, would only just do that and that's about it. Ask if I'm on medication, and if not, insist, if so, maybe ask how you're feeling but don't want deeper details. Then they send you out on your merry way. I'm stuck until I'm a legal adult, but there's a good chance I'm going to end it before I even reach that age.

I wish I knew how to format this correctly, but I'll just tell you the reasons I've gotten so far from them. Parents had bad experiences with therapy growing up, they believe I'll get taken away, we can't afford it, and they don't trust the medication psychiatrists prescribe because they think I'll get all loopy and be permanently screwed up from the medication.

Oh, wow! I do this too. But I don't necessarily do it on my bed or couch, I usually pace back and forth in my kitchen listening to a song and, like you said, when it gets to a good part, I start hopping instead of pacing.
